obligations.note: The changed line in service.py deliver_statement builds the log message from store.get_payee(payee_id).account_number, which the store unseals to plaintext. AppLog masks only keyword fields, not message text, so the full account number is logged on the delivery-failure path. The passing LOG-1 control test is a sample that does not exercise this path.
The LOG-1 deviation has no valid exception. The only LOG-1 exception, EXC-0167, is scoped to mortgage.logging (not payments.service) and only permits masked last-4 values.
service.py is in AUD-1 scope, but the change only edits a log call. The _audit call for deliver_statement is unchanged, and the registered AUD-1 control test passes on the head commit.
Ticket CHG-24472 is approved by change manager erik.brandt on 2026-10-19, before the change opened on 2026-10-21, and lists payments.service, the only component touched (service.py).
code_review approval by sofia.santos (change_approver for payments, a different person from author mara.costa per the directory).
The approval names head commit fdab983, the only commit in the change.

The CI run on head fdab983 passed the full payments suite (172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped), including the registered LOG-1 and AUD-1 control tests. Both are labelled sample, so their pass says little about this path.
The only touched path, service.py, maps to payments.service, which is not security_sensitive, so no security_review is required.
No protected paths (controls data, control tests, CI) are changed. The diff touches only apps/baseline-payments/payments/service.py.
The change and its ticket are standard (emergency=false), so no emergency PIR is due.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers service.py. The covered payments.py, audit.py, routes.py and Java files are unchanged, so no earlier evidence lapses.

summary: The change interpolates a payee's unsealed, full account number into an application error log message. AppLog masks only keyword fields, so the NPI is written unmasked, violating LOG-1. No approved, in-scope exception covers it, so EXC-1 also fails. The process records (ticket, independent approval of the head commit, green CI on head) are in order. The sample-based logging control test missed this path. Because LOG-1 is refuted, the change must be rejected.
